concept: size-matched KLD reporting for local quants
summary: llama.cpp's own scoreboard lists model size in GiB beside KLD for 40+ GGUF types of LLaMA 3 8B against an FP16 reference, sorted by KLD. A size-matched read needs no extra run.

facts.text: llama.cpp's own scoreboard lists model size in GiB beside KLD for 40+ GGUF types of LLaMA 3 8B against an FP16 reference, sorted by KLD. A size-matched read needs no extra run.
Equal-size pairs from that table (no imatrix unless stated): q5_0 and q5_K_S are both 5.21 GiB with KLD 0.022239 and 0.016595, so legacy q5_0 is 1.34 times worse at identical size.
q4_0 is 4.34 GiB with KLD 0.071940 while q4_K_S is 4.37 GiB with 0.043136: q4_0 is 0.7% smaller and 67% worse (q4_K_S is 40% lower).

Size ordering can invert quality ordering: q4_1 (4.78 GiB, KLD 0.071683) is 4.4% larger than q4_K_M (4.58 GiB, 0.031273) and 2.29 times worse; q5_1 (5.65 GiB, 0.018045) is 6.0% larger than q5_K_M (5.33 GiB, 0.010762) and 1.68 times worse.
A smaller file can tie a larger one: q3_K_L with the WT 10m imatrix (4.03 GiB, 0.073077) is 7.1% smaller than q4_0 (4.34 GiB, 0.071940) and within 1.6% of its KLD.

The importance matrix is a second axis at fixed size: q4_K_S at 4.37 GiB drops from 0.043136 (none) to 0.031951 (WT 10m), and q2_K at 2.96 GiB drops from 0.445132 (none) to 0.332223 (WT 10m), about 25%. Size-matching without matching imatrix status compares recipes, not formats.
The size of the imatrix corpus barely matters there: q2_K with 1k to 10m Wikitext tokens spans KLD 0.3321 to 0.3371, and the README says it sees no consistent improvement from more tokens.

Elasticity rule (derived): from q5_K_M to q4_K_M (5.33 to 4.58 GiB, -14%) KLD rises 2.9 times, and from q4_K_M to q3_K_M (4.58 to 3.74 GiB, -18%) it rises 3.3 times. The log-log slope is about -6 to -7, so on LLaMA 3 8B a 1% size gap corresponds to roughly 6 to 7% in KLD between 3- and 5-bit K-quants.

Consequence: a 3% size gap can masquerade as a 20% KLD gap, which is the size of difference vendors report between their quants and others. Report KLD together with size difference in percent, and treat a KLD gap smaller than the elasticity times the size gap as explained by size.

Baselines are large: the reference logits file for one 14B model on a 1.6 MiB corpus was about 55 GiB, and the guide suggests Q8_0 as the baseline if BF16 cannot be run. A Q8_0 baseline adds its own divergence floor (LLaMA 3 8B q8_0 mean KLD 0.001355), which is small beside 4-bit gaps but not beside 6-bit and 8-bit comparisons.

Record size in the llama.cpp record format: 2*((n_vocab+1)/2)+4 uint16 per scored position, about 256 KB per position at a 128,256-token vocabulary and about 304 KB at 151,936. A 55 GiB file is therefore about 190,000 scored positions at the larger vocabulary.
2024-01 onward: llama.cpp adds the KL-divergence mode (PR 5076, per the existing methodology dossier) and publishes LLaMA 2 and 3 scoreboards with sizes.
2025-05: ik_llama.cpp quant-cooking guide documents a two-pass KLD workflow on a custom corpus.
2026-02 to 2026-09: community and vendor tables move to size-adjusted scores (existing dossiers).
Elasticity is model-, family- and corpus-specific; the -6 to -7 figure comes from one 8B dense model on Wikitext and is a guide to magnitude, not a constant.
A table sorted by KLD with sizes in a separate column invites reading rank as quality; sort by size, plot the frontier, and mark dominated points.
Matching "within 1%" by file size can still mismatch loaded bytes: MLX files carry unquantized embeddings or vision towers (existing dossier), and GGUF mmproj files are separate.
Mean KLD and tail KLD can order the same two quants differently at equal size (existing Unsloth versus bartowski case), so a size-matched report needs both.

Equal size or equal label: vendors who tune tensor allocation argue for equal-size comparison (Unsloth), while critics compare same-name quants where the vendor file is smaller (existing dossier). The README data shows both can be right because a few percent in bytes moves KLD by tens of percent.
Mean KLD versus a size-adjusted composite score: a composite normalized against one baseline changes when the baseline changes; a frontier plot does not.
A KLD-versus-GiB frontier for GGUF and MLX quants of one BF16 base on one token stream on Apple silicon. None found.
Whether the log-log elasticity is stable across dense and MoE models and across 2- to 8-bit.
Whether KLD from Wikitext and KLD on agent traces rank equal-size quants the same way.
The llama.cpp LLaMA 3 8B scoreboard lists model size in GiB and KLD for each GGUF type against an FP16 reference, with imatrix variants.
In that scoreboard q5_0 and q5_K_S are both 5.21 GiB with KLD 0.022239 and 0.016595.
In that scoreboard q4_0 is 4.34 GiB at KLD 0.071940 and q4_K_S is 4.37 GiB at 0.043136.
In that scoreboard q4_1 is 4.78 GiB at KLD 0.071683, larger and worse than q4_K_M at 4.58 GiB and 0.031273.
In that scoreboard q5_1 is 5.65 GiB at KLD 0.018045, larger and worse than q5_K_M at 5.33 GiB and 0.010762.
In that scoreboard q3_K_L with the WT 10m imatrix is 4.03 GiB at KLD 0.073077, 7.1% smaller than q4_0 at nearly equal KLD.
In that scoreboard q4_K_S improves from KLD 0.043136 to 0.031951 and q2_K from 0.445132 to 0.332223 when an imatrix is added at unchanged file size.
The README states the f16 row shows only the difference from casting reference logits to 16-bit integers, with KLD 0.000551 on LLaMA 3 8B.
The ik_llama.cpp guide reports a KLD baseline file of about 55 GiB for Qwen3-14B BF16 on a 1.6 MiB corpus and suggests Q8_0 as baseline if BF16 cannot run.
On LLaMA 3 8B, KLD rises about 2.9 times from q5_K_M to q4_K_M and about 3.3 times from q4_K_M to q3_K_M, for size drops of 14% and 18%.
A size mismatch of a few percent between two 3- to 5-bit K-quants can explain a KLD difference of 20% or more.
A size-matched report should give size difference in percent, imatrix status, reference precision, corpus, and both mean and tail KLD.
